REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 14, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, AUGUST 14, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cub Scout Pack 529.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Saahas for Cause; United Indian Associations of So Cal; and Smita Vasant (South Asian
  Heritage Month).

  Asuncion "Annie" Dela Cruz (100th birthday).

  5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions, and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Tse, to approve Councilmember Hong’s
  nomination listed below for a two-year term of service, through April 30, 2027
  (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Grace Hu  Economic Development Commission

  (minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to appointee Grace Hu.

5C.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad hoc
  working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Linda Troxell, at the discretion of the Mayor, provided general public comments regarding
  her frustration with the current state of her home and requested assistance in securing
  toxic substance remediation services. General public comments are generally reserved for
  Agenda Item 6.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  No action was taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  David Pylman expressed concern and requested information regarding the Del Amo
  Bridge replacement and traffic signal synchronization project, including potential impacts
  from the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s Southeast Gateway
  Line (SEGL) Light Rail Project.

  Vicky Kirkwood expressed concern regarding the practice of banning books in public
  libraries.

  Sam Desai thanked the City Council for recognizing South Asian Heritage Month and
  offered suggestions for advising local business owners on how to navigate federal tariffs.

  Kirit Chauhan requested consideration of a future City event in recognition and
  celebration of South Asian heritage and culture.

  Catherine Pascual requested staff include additional context and clarity in future agenda
  reports related to the City’s ongoing water and sewer rate studies.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment submitted for Item 6, by the
  deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies
  of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business
  hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, July 28, 2025, 6:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Tse, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Monday, July 28,
  2025, 6:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 14, 2025 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Tse, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  August 14, 2025  $10,962,152.37 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency
  dated August 14, 2025 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Tse, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Register of

  Successor Agency  August 14, 2025  $6,639,454.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Adoption of Ordinance:

  Ordinance introduced at the Monday, July 28, 2025, City Council/Successor Agency
  Special Meeting:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1050, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 13.12 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADOPT
  THE CROSS-CONNECTION CONTROL POLICY HANDBOOK AS REQUIRED BY THE
  CALIFORNIA STATE WATER RESOURCES CONTROL BOARD* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this administrative activity is not a "project" under CEQA and is therefore
  exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Tse, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1050, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 13.12 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO ADOPT THE CROSS-CONNECTION CONTROL POLICY HANDBOOK AS
  REQUIRED BY THE CALIFORNIA STATE WATER RESOURCES CONTROL BOARD
  (COUNCIL); and

  2. Direct the City Clerk to publish a notice of adopted ordinance within fifteen (15) days
  after adoption of Ordinance No. 1050, as required by California Government Code
  Section 36933 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational report regarding existing City of Cerritos
  Municipal Code regulations pertaining to self-storage facilities (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Director of Community Development.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mike McCoy requested clarification regarding whether the local business community
  expressed an interest in additional self-storage facilities.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  ORIGINAL MOTION (DID NOT CARRY): It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by
  Pulido, to direct staff to:

  1. Initiate a development code amendment to Municipal Code Section 22.40.730(2)(b),
  formally removing the limitation prescribing that a maximum of four (4) self-storage
  facilities may operate within the City at any given time, and a CEQA environmental
  analysis for such an amendment;

  2. Present the development code amendment, related CEQA environmental analysis, and
  information regarding the 2024 sale of a self-storage facility located at 17900
  Crusader Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, to the Planning Commission at a future publicly
  noticed meeting; and

  3. Present the Planning Commission’s recommendations to the City Council at a future
  publicly noticed meeting (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to
  direct staff to prepare an expanded informational report, addressing current self-storage
  facility operating capacities and the details of the above-referenced 2024 sale, for City
  Council consideration at a future publicly noticed meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Johnson
  NOES:  Pulido, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an informational report on the Sister City program history
  and designation policy (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, Director of Community and Cultural Services.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Adrian Ayub shared a personal anecdote of his experience hosting a Japanese exchange
  student and expressed concern regarding the tangible benefits of a Sister City program.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Pulido, to receive and file this report
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION TO RECONSIDER A VOTE TAKEN AT THIS MEETING

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to reconsider the vote
  taken earlier in this meeting generally described as the preparation of an expanded
  informational report concerning self-storage facilities (COUNCIL) (the specific motion and
  vote to be reconsidered is detailed on Page 5 of this document).

  The motion to reconsider the vote described in the motion above carried (5 – 0), as
  follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  RECONSIDER OF VOTE ON SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES

  The matter under consideration is described on the agenda and within the agenda report,
  as follows:

  Agenda Item 9A.:  Review and consideration of an informational report regarding
  existing City of Cerritos Municipal Code regulations pertaining to
  self-storage facilities (COUNCIL).

  The matter may be discussed and debated as if it were on the floor for the first time. If
  no new motion is put forth, it would stand as if action on the matter under consideration
  never occurred.

  NEW MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to
  direct staff to:

  1. Prepare an agenda report, for consideration by the Planning Commission at a future
  publicly noticed meeting, inclusive of:

  a. A development code amendment to Municipal Code Section 22.40.730, formally
  removing the limitation prescribing that a maximum of four (4) self-storage
  facilities may operate within the City at any given time;

  b. Information regarding the 2024 sale of a self-storage facility located at 17900
  Crusader Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703;

  c. An overview of the four (4) existing self-storage facilities operating within the
  City, inclusive of rental rates, square footage, number of units, and percentage
  capacity;

  d. A comprehensive history of City Council action related to the existing Municipal
  Code regulations on self-storage facilities; and

  2. Present the Planning Commission’s recommendations to the City Council at a future
  publicly noticed meeting (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Tse and Hong, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and
  Mayor Yokoyama.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to provide a memorandum to
  the City Council identifying cost-saving opportunities in the Cerritos Library’s operational
  (non-personnel) budget.

12.  Closed Session

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to

  Unrepresented Employees: Full-Time Exempt
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 14, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 8 of 8

  12C.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - POTENTIAL LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of Potential Cases: One (1)

  The City Council recessed into Closed Session.

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session.

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  The City Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A, 12B, and 12C. There

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:30 p.m.
